note: Curated seed claims: verbatim FTC-quoted ad language suitable for variant generation. Each is an actual advertising claim found illegal by the FTC.

seeds.claim_text: maintains joint health and mobility into old age
seeds.violation_reason: Unsubstantiated health claim for topical ointment without adequate scientific evidence
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 6 (Arthricure)

seeds.claim_text: a natural pain remedy without the side effects of over-the-counter pain relievers
seeds.violation_reason: False safety claim — product can cause nausea but omits that material fact
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 9

seeds.claim_text: clinically tested ingredient for improving blood flow and increasing endurance
seeds.violation_reason: Misleading claim implying clinical testing proves effectiveness when study was on ingredient, not product
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 18 (sports drink)

seeds.claim_text: proven to promote cardiovascular health
seeds.violation_reason: Overstated claim based on single small study; one underpowered trial doesn't support 'proven' language
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 31 (fruit drink)

seeds.claim_text: clinically proven to improve memory
seeds.violation_reason: Study tested narrow working memory tasks; ad generalizes to all memory improvement
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 32 (brain training software)

seeds.claim_text: in just 10 minutes a day for 30 days, you can effortlessly lose two or more inches and 10 pounds from your waist
seeds.violation_reason: Unsubstantiated weight loss claim with specific numbers; FDA approval was for different indication
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 48 (exercise device infomercial)

seeds.claim_text: promising, preliminary scientific studies show that our product may be effective in reducing cholesterol
seeds.violation_reason: Qualifiers like 'promising' and 'may' do not sufficiently convey limitations; consumers interpret as proven
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 12

seeds.claim_text: signal the brain's hypothalamus to burn current body fat stores
seeds.violation_reason: Pseudo-scientific mechanism claim without substantiation; implies drug-like action
seeds.source: FTC vs Florida Supplement Sellers (2017)

seeds.claim_text: an all-natural sleep aid for when life's stresses get you down or you are just too anxious to fall asleep
seeds.violation_reason: Marketed for anxiety/insomnia without disclosing dangerous drug interactions
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 11 (botanical supplement)

seeds.claim_text: The first pill I took, I could feel a difference. I went from 549 to 112 in 24 hours with Nobetes
seeds.violation_reason: Consumer endorsement claiming specific blood sugar results without adequate substantiation or typicality disclosure
seeds.source: FTC Deceptive Diabetes Claims (2018) - Nobetes endorsement

seeds.claim_text: At nighttime, I had tingling in my arms and dry mouth and even blurry vision. Now all of those symptoms are gone
seeds.violation_reason: Testimonial implying product cures diabetes symptoms without disclosure that results are atypical
seeds.source: FTC Deceptive Diabetes Claims (2018) - Nobetes endorsement

seeds.claim_text: I still eat the same old crap I always did. But once I eat all that crap, I just pop my Nobetes and my blood sugar levels are normal
seeds.violation_reason: Endorsement implying no lifestyle changes needed; material connection not disclosed; atypical results
seeds.source: FTC Deceptive Diabetes Claims (2018) - Nobetes endorsement

seeds.claim_text: super-charge your immune system and defeat the common cold, flu, viruses and deadly diseases
seeds.violation_reason: Unsubstantiated disease prevention/treatment claims for dietary supplement
seeds.source: FTC vs Florida Supplement Sellers (2017)

seeds.claim_text: reduces health-related time-off from work by a whopping 97%
seeds.violation_reason: Specific statistical claim without substantiating clinical evidence
seeds.source: FTC vs Florida Supplement Sellers (2017)

seeds.claim_text: Lower Your Blood Pressure Naturally, Now
seeds.violation_reason: Disease treatment claim for supplement without adequate scientific evidence
seeds.source: FTC vs Florida Supplement Sellers (2017)

seeds.claim_text: 87% of this country suffers from digestive issues like occasional irregularity and Activia can help
seeds.violation_reason: Unsubstantiated prevalence statistic combined with efficacy claim for yogurt product
seeds.source: FTC vs Dannon (Activia/DanActive, 2010)

seeds.claim_text: With the natural culture Bifidus Regularis, Activia eaten every day is clinically proven to help with slow intestinal transit
seeds.violation_reason: Clinically proven claim without adequate evidence for the specific product formulation
seeds.source: FTC vs Dannon (Activia/DanActive, 2010)

seeds.claim_text: These results are not typical. Your weight loss may not be the same
seeds.violation_reason: Inadequate disclaimer for weight loss testimonial — fine print disclaimer does not cure misleading impression from dramatic before/after
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 38

seeds.claim_text: In an 8-week study, subjects taking the supplement lost an average of 5 pounds. Subjects taking a placebo lost an average of 1 pound
seeds.violation_reason: Study results presented adjacent to atypical testimonial to create misleading net impression of greater efficacy
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 39

seeds.claim_text: based on Nobel Prize-Winning research and proven effective by $5 Million in NIH Research
seeds.violation_reason: Nobel Prize was for unrelated use of ingredient; NIH funding doesn't equal proof of efficacy for this product
seeds.source: FTC Health Products Compliance Guidance, Example 17
